text:
maria: Hey team — customer in DE reporting a spike of 401s and 250-400ms additional tail latency starting ~08:10 UTC. They say traffic is landing in us-central instead of eu-west. Can someone help triage? :rotating_light:
ashok: Can you paste a couple of example request IDs + the client IPs you see in their debug headers? Also want a dig + EDNS output from their office if possible. Suspect ECS strip or ISP cache. :thinking:
mike: Pasting what we got from customer (redacted):
```
curl -i "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" -H "X-Client-IP: 85.214.132.45"
Response headers: x-pop: us-central1, x-auth: 401, x-request-id: req_20240317_0001
```
There are multiple recent request_ids with x-pop showing us-central1.
maria: Here's a dig we asked them to run from their office (Frankfurt):
```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> api.redwood.ai +short +short
;; global options: +cmd
api.redwood.ai.  60 IN A 34.85.12.4
;; OPT PSEUDOSECTION:
; EDNS: version: 0, flags:; udp: 1232
; CLIENT-SUBNET: 0.0.0.0/0 -> 34.85.12.4
```
mike: That looks like the resolver returned a US IP. TTL is 60s which is short but enough to survive caches. Customer mentioned their ISP (TeleKom regional) recently rolled a resolver update.
dashok: Ops, can you check our GeoIP DB sync timestamps and the edge-pop-assignment logs for those request_ids? If GeoIP DB is stale or our hostname-to-pop mapping rolled back, that would explain the us-pop answers.
ops-sre: Looking now — our geoip sync job hit a 503 from the S3 source at 07:58 UTC and retried. Latest successful sync prior to the incident was 03:02 UTC. There's a retry window that could have left some nodes with older DB entries.
daniela: Also seeing a small surge of ECS-stripped resolvers in the telemetry (eds strip rate increased ~07:50), likely ISP-side edns-client-subnet removal. When ECS is missing we fallback to resolver IP geolocation which for some ISPs maps to a transit exit in the US. That would cause correct auth tokens tied to eu regions to be rejected (401) if we route to a different cluster.
mike: Customer reported a billing spike for token auth failures (retries) — asked to open a billing case. I'm marking this as P1 for support escalation because it's customer impacting and billing.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20240317-27 (channel: #support, severity: P1)
ashok: Quick repro I ran from a US VPN: dig shows A -> us IP. Repro steps for eng: 1) emulate resolver with ECS stripped 2) query api.redwood.ai 3) observe pop assignment mismatch and x-pop header.
ashok: Possible mitigation options: - force-pop-routing on incoming requests based on X-Client-IP header for known enterprise ranges (temporary) - roll forward geoip DB from backup to edges that failed to sync - increase TTL on DNS answers (but that won't help immediate drift)
daniela: We should avoid increasing TTL immediately (can make cache misalignment worse). Short-term: push geoip re-sync and invalidate local pop mapping cache on affected edges; long-term: detect ECS-strip and prefer AS-to-region hints or client IP header if present for enterprise customers.
ops-sre: I'm triggering a manual geoip refresh to edges that failed the sync and invalidating the pop-assignment cache. Doing a controlled rollout to eu-west nodes first.
maria: Customer on call now — can we try forcing a retry routing to eu-west for affected request_ids? If they hit eu-west and auth succeeds, that's a good repro confirmation.
ops-sre: I've added a temporary routing override for the customer's ASN to prefer eu-west for the next 15 minutes. Watch for request_ids to flip.
mike: Customer reports 2 of 3 requests now show x-pop: eu-west1 and auth succeeded. They still see occasional us answers but much reduced. :thumbsup:
daniela: Filing an engineering follow-up: make ECS strip detection feed into routing policy and add a safety check for auth-pop mismatch to avoid billing-causing retries.
ashok: I'll open a draft RFC for a fallback policy: if auth fails and x-pop !== expected_region, attempt controlled retry to pinned-region before returning 401 to client.
maria: Thanks team. Next steps: ops-sre to confirm full refresh completed; eng to own the RFC; support to file billing case and collect request_ids. I'll keep the customer updated.
ops-sre: Geoip refresh completed across affected edges at 08:30 UTC, edge cache invalidations pushed. Monitoring for drift.
support-l2: Billing case opened with ACCT-9843, added request_ids and timeline.
maria: Great — closing the P1 after monitoring period if no more regressions. Thanks everyone. :heart:
